summary.headline: Jungle Camps Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, but EBITDA fell to ₹1.69 cr (27% margin) after a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 12% YoY to ₹5.97 cr, with occupancy up 2 pts to 45% and RevPAR up 9% to ₹4,763. EBITDA declined to ₹1.69 cr from ₹1.81 cr and margin compressed to 27% from 32%, partly from new-property ramp-up costs and a ₹0.52 cr exceptional charge tied to the discontinued Parsili project. PAT fell to ₹0.47 cr from ₹1.13 cr. Management outlined Devprayag and Palash Kothi (42 rooms combined) as FY27 additions, Mathura (105 rooms, IHG Holiday Inn Express) and Sheopur Fort (35–40 rooms in phase 1) for FY28, and a debt build-up to about ₹50 cr by FY28.

guidance_outlook: ADR expected to be better in October–March than the current run-rate; management said it is 'quite hopeful' of ~5% ADR growth for FY27 but gave no formal number.
Second half (October–March) margins expected to be better than the same period last year.
Devprayag (Uttarakhand, 22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism Board) to start in Q2 FY27; ADR guided at ₹5,000–6,000; capex up to ₹1 cr; lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

Mathura (IHG Holiday Inn Express, scaled to 105 rooms) targeted for FY28 opening; revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ₹12 cr; project cost ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; lease rental 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever higher.

Sheopur Fort (60-key heritage hotel, 90-year lease, competitive bid) to open 35–40 rooms in 1H FY28 with the rest in FY29; budget ₹25 cr (₹10.5 cr internal, ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan); first-year revenue expected at least ₹12 cr.
Kukru Jungle Camp (Melghat, 15–20 tents, ₹7–7.5 cr capex) expected operational by end-FY28 (March 2028).
Debt expected to reach around ₹50 cr by end-FY28 per Q&A; Mathura and Sheopur loans have 2-year moratorium then 7-year repayment, combined EMI about ₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 cr/yr).
Management expects EBITDA margin around 30% over time, but new properties dilute margin until stabilised; new properties take roughly 4–6 months, up to 6 months, to stabilise.
capex_capacity: Current portfolio 8 operational properties with 137 keys (3 owned, 5 leased/managed); 4 pipeline properties.

Mathura: planned capacity expanded from 60 to 105 rooms plus banqueting and dining; project cost ₹49 cr; partly funded by ₹11.5 cr IPO component and ₹32 cr HDFC loan; ₹8.79 cr already invested in subsidiary Madhuvan Hospitality.
Sheopur Fort: development commenced; ₹3.5 cr spent on Sheopur and Pench renovation under CWIP; ₹7 cr standalone tangible assets increase YoY largely CWIP.
Parsili project discontinued after regulatory constraints; ₹1.22 cr premium refundable, ₹0.50 cr performance security to be returned; IPO proceeds redeployed to Sheopur.
Panna, Satpura, Sariska and Jawai at advanced/exploration stage; Ratapani land held, construction expected to start shortly.
demand_pricing: Seasonality: safari season October–March drives ADR and revenue; April–June slower; park closed June/July–September, properties remain open with discounts.
Management said occupancy ceiling is about 60% in wildlife, citing Tadoba at 57%; FY26 occupancy 40%.
Management said competition has not yet hurt ADR or margins, positioning on naturalist-led experience rather than five-star luxury.
Holiday Express brand chosen for Mathura; IHG fee structure of around 7–8% of revenue across four or five components.

qa_highlights.question: What ADR growth can be expected for full-year FY27, given Q1 ADR up ~5% YoY and H2 seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed October–March (H2) should deliver better ADR and revenue than April–June, but gave no formal FY27 number; it said it is 'quite hopeful' of ~5% YoY ADR growth. FY26 property ADRs cited: Pench ₹9,248, Tadoba ₹12,300, Kanha ₹9,500, Rukhad ₹11,800, Bison ₹3,500.

qa_highlights.question: Is 40% FY26 occupancy low, and can it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the park is closed for about three months (July–September), so 40% is ~54% on the open period; wildlife occupancy tops out near 60%, with Tadoba at 57%. Mathura and other new properties are expected to lift the numbers, with a 12-month operating model for Mathura and Sheopur.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA spike in FY27 or stay flat, and how quickly do new properties break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Devprayag and Palash Kothi will add top-line and bottom-line growth this year. New properties take about 4–6 months, up to 6 months, to stabilise, and management agreed break-even around six months after commissioning is a fair read.

qa_highlights.question: What are the revenue terms for Palash Kothi and Devprayag, and what ADRs are guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Palash Kothi (20 rooms, Bandhavgarh) pays Jungle Camps a 13% revenue fee and operates October to June, ADR ₹8,000–12,000. Devprayag (22 rooms, leased from UP Tourism) starts in Q2 FY27 with ADR ₹5,000–6,000, capex up to ₹1 cr, and lease rental ₹28,000 per year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt build-up, interest rate and repayment schedule for Mathura and Sheopur?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura project cost is ₹49 cr with ₹32 cr HDFC debt at 8.14%; Sheopur budget ₹25 cr with ~₹17.5 cr HDFC loan and ₹10.5 cr internal. Both loans have a 2-year moratorium then 7-year repayment, combined EMI ~₹53 lakh/month (~₹6.5 cr/yr). Management said debt reaching ~₹50 cr by FY28 is correct and no working capital debt is needed.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from Mathura and Sheopur, and is debt serviceable at downside?
qa_highlights.answer: Mathura revenue estimate ₹18–20 cr/yr, with management comfortable even at ~₹12 cr. Sheopur first-year revenue at least ₹12 cr on ~35 rooms, with 8–10 weddings a year and ~15% other occupancy cited as a cushion. Mathura lease rental is 5% of gross revenue or ₹54 lakh, whichever is higher.

qa_highlights.question: How were the two land-related incidents (Parsili and a second site) handled, and what due-diligence changes followed?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹70–75 lakh was invested in the first site; ~₹50 lakh is being written off, with some assets moved to another property. Management said due diligence now includes forest department engagement upfront and checks of revenue, police and court records. It said there is no significant challenge at Sheopur or Mathura, but development timelines apply.

risks_watch: Execution on Mathura (105 rooms, FY28) and Sheopur (35–40 rooms in 1H FY28): both are bank-funded and analysts flagged a possible one-to-two-quarter delay.
Debt rising to ~₹50 cr by FY28 against a small base (FY26 PAT ₹4.22 cr), with combined EMIs of ~₹6.5 cr/yr from the 2-year moratorium ending.
Margin dilution from new properties (ramp-up 4–6 months, up to 6 months) versus management's ~30% target; Q1 margin fell to 27% from 32%.
Land and title risk: a forest-linked issue and a land dispute led to a write-off (~₹50 lakh) and ₹1.35 cr received of the amount due, with a suit filed on the balance.
Lease terms for Sheopur (competitive bid, 90-year lease) and Devprayag; management said no cancellation clause if the property is developed, but the risk of renegotiation was raised.
Kukru (Melghat) still awaiting permissions and water infrastructure; operational target end-FY28 (March 2028).
Parsili refund: ₹1.22 cr premium plus ₹0.50 cr performance security to be returned; management said it could come 'at any time now', with GST not refunded.
Investor relations: an institutional investor complained that requested information was still outstanding after 2–3 months; the company said it would follow up.
key_quotes: So, these 2 properties were very small. It has 8 rooms, it is on the highway, but its tariff is very low.
In the beginning, it takes 4 -6 months for a property.
We are expecting, we are quite hopeful.
Both loans have a two-year moratorium, followed by a seven-year repayment period.
Even if the revenue is around ₹12 crore, we would still be comfortable.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the pipeline, funding and the 30% margin target, but cautious and hedged on FY27 ADR (said only 'quite hopeful' of ~5%) and gave no formal full-year number. It was evasive on several specifics: the Sheopur lease cancellation question, the outstanding IR request, and the timing of the Parsili refund.
